## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to compose shifts and OR to implement rotate without loops or conditionals, a common low-level operation.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts and wrap-around semantics
- 32-bit boundary, undefined behavior avoidance
- Performance and portability considerations

## Code Example

```javascript
function rotl32(n, k) {
  return ((n << k) | (n >>> (32 - k))) >>> 0;
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- What happens if k === 0? How does the expression evaluate?
- How would you implement rotate-right similarly?
- How would you adapt for 64-bit values in a language without native unsigned support?

## Why This Is Asked
This checks understanding of 128-bit bit rotations using only shifts and masks, with a branch-free formula.

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise shifts and modulo wrap-around
- 128-bit arithmetic and safe shifts
- Branch-free expression design

## Code Example
```c
uint128 rotateRight128(uint128 x, uint64_t r){
  r &= 127; // 0..127
  return (x >> r) | (x << ((128 - r) % 128));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for rotate left? 
- What happens if r is large or negative input?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of cross-lane bit manipulation and wrap-around across a 128-bit value.

## Key Concepts
- 128-bit split across two uint64 halves
- Cross-lane bit movement with shifts
- Non-branching bitwise updates

## Code Example

```c
uint128 rotateLeft128_1(uint128 x) {
  uint64_t new_lo = (x.lo << 1) | (x.hi >> 63);
  uint64_t new_hi = (x.hi << 1) | (x.lo >> 63);
  uint128 r; r.hi = new_hi; r.lo = new_lo; return r;
}
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests the ability to pack multiple fields into a single word, a common task in serialization and network protocols. It emphasizes precise bit-width handling and avoiding branches.

## Key Concepts

- Bitwise masking
- Bit shifts
- Field packing into a 32-bit word

## Code Example

```javascript
function packHeader(version, flags, length) {
  return ((version & 0x0F) << 28) | ((flags & 0xFF) << 20) | (length & 0xFFFFF);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extract version, flags, and length from the header?
- How would you validate inputs to prevent overflow or sign issues in languages with signed integers?
